transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because after everyone goes to bed, I’ll think I’m just going to have some leftovers, and then it turns into a lot. Like, I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks are in the pantry—all in one sitting.
During these nighttime eating episodes, are you fully awake and aware of what you're doing, or do you sometimes not remember eating until you see the evidence the next morning?
I’m not really sure how to tell. I know I eat at night, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether I remember every part of it afterward.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating once you start?

Yes. Once I start—especially if I’ve had a tense night with my husband—it feels like the part of me that makes decisions just goes offline. I keep reaching for more even while I’m telling myself, “Patricia, stop. This is enough.”
When these episodes happen, is it because you haven't gone to sleep yet and are still up in the evening, or do you find that you actually wake up from sleep and then start eating?
I’m not sure, honestly. I know it’s at night, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m already awake or if I wake up and then go eat.
The next morning after one of these nighttime eating episodes, do you find that you have little to no appetite and eat much less than usual, especially early in the day?
I’m not sure, to be honest. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m eating less the next morning or not.
Has your husband ever seen you eating at night, and if so, did he say you looked awake and responsive, or more like you were asleep or in a trance?
I honestly don’t know. We haven’t really talked about whether he’s seen me, or what I looked like at the time.
The next morning, when you think back on the eating episode from the night before, do you clearly remember deciding to eat and what you ate, or is it more like a hazy or blank memory?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to how clearly I remember it the next morning.
During these nighttime eating episodes, have you or your husband ever noticed you eating something unusual—like raw or frozen food, or even non-food items—that you wouldn't normally eat?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed eating anything like that, and I don’t know if my husband has either.
During these nighttime eating episodes, are you fully awake and able to think, talk, and respond normally, or do you feel more like you're in a daze or not fully alert?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m fully alert or more out of it when it happens.

Before you start eating at night, are you already lying awake—like unable to fall asleep or having trouble sleeping—or does the eating seem to happen without you being consciously aware you were awake beforehand?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed whether I’m lying awake beforehand or if it just happens without me being aware of waking up.
Aside from these nighttime episodes, do you ever have similar times during the day where you feel like you can't stop eating once you start?

Yes. Especially after a tense night with my husband, once I start eating, it feels like the part of me that makes decisions just goes offline. I keep reaching for more even while I’m telling myself, “Patricia, stop, this is enough.”
